       Questions 1-5

       Match each message (1-5) and its meaning (A-F).

       Mark your answer on the answer sheet.
       There is an example at the beginning (0→G).


  0      When you come to London, there’s no need for you to book into a hotel. You can sleep
         at my place.

  1      She should apologise to me. I didn’t start it but when she yelled at me I didn’t shut up. I have
         no regrets. You should be proud of me.

  2      I have to tell you something. I’ve read your poems. They’re great, so sensitive and deep. My
         girl is a real poet. I love being your mum.

  3      You can’t ignore the reality. Being honest is hard but I’ll be with you when you break the news
         to him. The sooner you do it, the better you’ll feel.

  4      Your last drawings are really fantastic. Everybody can see that. Don’t listen to what your
         classmates say. They don’t get it anyway. I think they’re probably jealous of your talent.

  5      No one has to know what you’re going through right now. People have no clue about anything.
         Keep it to yourself for your own good. Just trust me.

Task 2
       Questions 6-10

       You will read five emails.
       For each question (6-10), choose the correct answer (A, B or C).
       Mark your answer on the answer sheet.


  6      Dear Ms Bates,
         This is Charles from the Pet Shop. About your order for 20 kg of Bonzo food. Unfortunately,
         that particular brand only comes in 15 kg bags, or 30 kg bags. Could you please tell us which
         size you would prefer, or if you’d rather order a different brand. Please don’t hesitate to call me
         if you have any questions.
         Kind regards,
         Charles Winter

         How much dog food does Ms Bates need?

         A 15 kg.
         B 20 kg.
         C 30 kg.



  7      Hi Frank,
         I showed Linda the plan of our trip. She wasn’t exactly thrilled about having to spend a third
         night in Frankfurt in that super expensive hotel. Not that I mind too much! And she had some
         questions about the schedule on Day 1, which certainly looks very busy. But in the end she
         gave it the green light.
         Sara

         What did Linda think of the plan?

         A She wasn’t happy about it.
         B She was unsure about it.
         C She agreed with it.

      I really think we should make a trip and visit Nick. It’s not an excuse to get out of town for a
      while, I promise. It’s just that I spoke to him yesterday and I didn’t like the sound of his voice.
      Not one little bit. We could get lunch on the way at your favourite restaurant. What do you
      think?

      A To get out of town.
      B She’s worried about Nick.
      C To eat in her favourite restaurant.



  9   Hi John,
      Sorry I haven’t been in touch for so long. Things have been busy as always. Work, the kids,
      and so on. Normal stuff. And also, I don’t know, I suppose I’m just a bit sad. Maybe I’m just sick
      and tired of things. Lucy thinks I should look around for a different job. Who knows? See you
      soon, anyway.
      Ben

      What does Ben say about himself?

      B He’s feeling down.
      C He’s been unwell.



 10   Bill,
      Have you packed for the weekend? I don’t know about you, but I can’t wait – 2 days in the

Task 3
       Questions 11-15

       Read the text below.
       For each question (11-15), choose the correct answer (A, B, or C).
       Mark your answer on the answer sheet.


                                         Award Winning Stuntman

      Everybody loves a good action movie. The amazing tricks and adrenaline-pumping action scenes
  are mesmerizing, mainly because many of us couldn’t imagine doing them. Many actors don’t want
  to risk their necks for these show-stopping stunts, either. Instead, movies often rely on stuntmen to
  make sure the movie is action-packed.
      Alejandro Garcia, with over 300 movies to his credit, has earned recognition as one of the
  industry’s top stuntmen. His parents were poor immigrants. Alejandro was born in 1982, and a year
  later they decided to leave New Mexico. And a year after that they went to seek their fortune in Los
  Angeles. His twin sisters were born two years later and they all made brilliant careers in the movie
  business, even his much younger brother Enrique.
      In the beginning, Alejandro’s parents didn’t support his childhood dream to become an actor. So,
  after graduating from school he considered becoming a baker. However, it was clear to everybody
  that he was destined for more exciting things, so he started working as a lifeguard. Soon, he was
  offered a small role in an action movie and moved to Hollywood. The stuntman on the set got sick
  and Alejandro performed the stunt himself. From then on, his career took a new turn.
      This eight-time winner of the Taurus World Stunt Award has worked with many brilliant directors,
  who helped him develop both personally and professionally. And he’s made a fortune, too. Back
  in the early 2000s, when he started out, a daily rate was $600. Nowadays, however, top stuntmen
  like Alejandro get paid up to $5000, depending on the stunt. But the average is $1000 a day for a
  beginner.
      During the course of his career Alejandro ended up in hospital many times. He broke 56 bones,
  including his back, dislocated a shoulder three times, knocked out several teeth and punctured a
  lung, which almost cost him his life. Still, he didn’t give up.



 11      When did Alejandro move to Los Angeles?

         A In 1982.
         B In 1983.
         C In 1984.

                                                Ghost nets

      Fishing nets used to be made from rope. But since the 1960s, they are made from nylon,
  (0) ___. Nylon is plastic and it does not break down. That means that fishing nets lost in the ocean,
  called ghost nets, (16) ___. Because of this, hundreds of millions of marine animals are killed or
  injured every year.
      Ghost nets injure and kill marine animals and fish that become trapped. There is plenty of life
  around abandoned fishing nets, (17) ___. Sea turtles look for floating objects to hide under them
  (18) ___. But turtles do not know that ghost nets are not safe for them and they get caught.
      The problem of ghost nets has been known for years but (19) ___. Even though one of them,
  Fishing Ltd, did mention the problem, there were no reports on it. Moreover, it’s impossible
  to identify which ship a ghost net comes from. This is why (20) ___, which mainly occurs in
  international waters. Unfortunately, as long as there is no effective international control system,
  fishing ships can continue to leave their old nets in the sea without punishment.
